tagline: Fifteen miles up a watershed canyon to the ski country.
intro: The byway starts at the mouth of the canyon, minutes from downtown Salt Lake City, and the city gives way quickly. The walls close in, and SR-190 climbs the V-shaped canyon that Big Cottonwood Creek cut, past trailheads, picnic grounds and old water and mining works, to the ski country at the top.

The creek is the reason for the rules. The canyon supplies drinking water to the Wasatch Front, so dogs and other domestic animals stay home. In summer the road keeps going past Brighton, over Guardsman Pass toward Park City.

moments.title: Stairs Station
moments.text: A Second Renaissance Revival powerhouse of 1894 and 1895 that once spun four Pelton wheels and now holds a single turbine, an intact high-head plant of the late 19th century.

moments.title: Solitude
moments.text: Robert M. Barrett, a uranium man from Moab, started this ski area in 1956 after Alta refused him the use of its restrooms.

moments.title: Brighton
moments.text: Skiing here began in 1936, when members of the Alpine Ski Club built a rope tow out of wire and an old elevator motor.

practical: The canyon is a protected watershed and domestic animals are not allowed. The road beyond Brighton over Guardsman Pass is normally closed all winter.
